title: Adaptive Intervals under Missing-at-Random Outcomes with Unknown Rare Arrival Floors
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; conditional ordered-gap converse lacks an evaluated rate, concrete admissible sequence, and matching q-free honest interval.
gap_reasons: The note proves a conditional finite-sample witness-subclass lower bound proportional to an unevaluated ordered moment gap, but it establishes neither the magnitude of that gap nor any concrete asymptotic regime in which the total-variation condition holds and the bound creates a material adaptation penalty.

With the gridwise Pareto frontiers, matching intervals, and q-free procedures all open, the delivered package is a technically nontrivial but narrow implicit converse rather than a field-level adaptive-rate result.
proof_attempt_summary: The D pipeline developed a finite-sample conditional honest-interval lower bound using ordered moment duality and membership-preserving cross-class witnesses, then transferred it to a Kallus–Mao-style ambient MAR slice. The D0.5 math panel passed, but the tier panel graded the result incremental: the ordered gap was not evaluated, and no concrete material-penalty regime or matching q-free interval was proved. Discovery stopped below the required field floor before Lean formalization.
tldr: The arrival floor is a class label rather than a uniformly estimable nuisance when occupied cells can have arbitrarily small mass. For two nested randomized finite-cell MAR classes, an ordered reciprocal moment gap and a proof-only activation augmentation produce close fuzzy hypotheses while retaining every observed enrollment membership; a deterministic projection returns the exact observed record. The headline theorem lower-bounds favorable-class expected length for every connected interval honest on the rough class. A new witness-subclass corollary verifies the Kallus--Mao-style potential-outcome MAR, treatment-overlap, binary-outcome, arrival-floor, and observed-record conditions on those same fuzzy hypotheses and transfers the identical \(\Delta_{n,d}(q_+,q_-)\) lower bound under the identical \(\eta_{n,d}(q_+,q_-)\) condition to the broader ambient criterion. The complete finite randomized and ambient model classes are generally incomparable; the lower-bound witnesses lie in their intersection. The gridwise point-risk and grid-honest expected-length Pareto frontiers and matching multiscale procedures remain open.
gap: Known-floor rare-arrival procedures tune their polynomial degree, light-cell threshold, and uncertainty radius to a declared floor. With no minimum cell mass, the smallest occupied-cell arrival probability is not uniformly estimable. Existing adaptation theory does not evaluate the complete-likelihood distance between nested finite-cell MAR classes.
fill: The ordered reciprocal moment program and a proof-only activation experiment give a computable two-class lower frontier; a deterministic Markov projection carries its distance bound to the exact observed experiment. The open construction targets two explicit simultaneous regions: classwise MSE for one estimator not given the true floor, and classwise maximal expected length for one connected interval honest on every grid class.
